Abstract:
Academic credential verification is fundamental to admissions, employment, and professional licensing. 
Traditional methods rely on manual checks and centralized databases, making them slow, costly, and vulnerable 
to document forgery. This paper presents Vardox — a public-blockchain anchored academic credential verification 
architecture. Institutions digitally sign certificates, generate SHA-256 cryptographic hashes, and anchor these 
proofs immutably on Ethereum via smart contracts. Original documents are stored off-chain while the blockchain 
serves as a tamper-proof source of truth. A QR-code-based interface simplifies verification for non-technical 
users. The system is built using Ethereum, Solidity, Next.js, and Node.js. Experimental results demonstrate 
improved verification accuracy, reduced verification time, and strong resistance to document tampering compared

Introduction Preventing DOS & MITM Attacks On Sensors Used In Smart Cities
Sensors are increasingly integrated into modern systems like smart cities, making their security a major concern. They continuously gather, transmit, and analyze data to enable real-time decision-making and automation. Due to exposure to open environments and wireless communication, sensors are highly vulnerable to cyberattacks such as DoS, spoofing, and data tampering. Motivation Growing reliance on sensor-based systems in smart infrastructure, and industrial control networks.
Sensors are critical for automated decision-making; their compromise can cause safety, financial, and operational risks.
Real-world incidents show attackers can easily exploit unsecured sensor networks.
Lack of standardized security frameworks and limitations of traditional defenses increase vulnerability.
Project aims to develop lightweight, real-time, and effective security measures.

Problem Statement Smart cities depend on sensors (GPS, LiDAR, cameras, etc.) for traffic management, navigation, and public safety.
These sensors are exposed to open environments, making them vulnerable to cyberattacks such as Denial of Service (DoS) and Man-in-the-Middle (MITM). Abstract This project is about detecting deepfake images using a combination of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Vision Transformers (ViT). The goal is not only to identify fake images correctly but also to clearly show how the system makes its decisions. The CNN part focuses on small facial details such as unnatural textures and minor visual errors, while the ViT part looks at the complete face to understand overall patterns and relationships between different facial areas. In addition to this, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is used to find hidden manipulation patterns that are difficult to detect using normal image analysis. To make the output easy for users to understand, Grad-CAM is used to generate heatmaps that highlight the facial regions responsible for the final prediction. The entire system is developed as a web-based application, allowing users to upload images and check whether they are real or fake. The model was tested on commonly used deepfake datasets, and the results show that this combined approach works better than using a single model. Overall, this project provides a simple, practical, and easy-to-use solution to deal with the growing problem of deepfake media in the digital world. ABSTRACT The ability to identify land-use types accurately based on aerial imagery is a vital component of physical planning, environmental assessment, and infrastructure upkeep. Early identification of key land-use categories such as roads, buildings, vegetation, and water bodies enables better planning and informed decision-making. However, traditional manual interpretation of land-use types within Geographic Information System (GIS) software is often time-consuming and inconsistent due to variations in the analyst’s expertise. To address these challenges, this project introduces an Automated Land-Use Classification and Segmentation System using Deep Learning. The proposed system leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to perform both multi-class classification and semantic segmentation on aerial imagery. A publicly available labeled dataset is preprocessed and used to train the model, enabling accurate detection and categorization of land features. The system also includes an interactive dashboard that visually represents segmented outputs, overlays detected features on input images, and displays confidence scores through intuitive graphs and statistics. This integrated approach ensures improved accuracy, efficiency, and consistency in land-use analysis. The proposed solution demonstrates a scalable and practical method for automated geospatial analysis, supporting urban planning, environmental monitoring, and infrastructure management with minimal human intervention. It is specifically designed to automatically learn and extract important features from images without the need for manual feature engineering. CNNs are highly effective in recognizing patterns such as edges, textures, shapes, and objects within an image. A CNN consists of multiple layers, each performing a specific function. The convolutional layer is responsible for extracting features by applying filters to the input image. These filters detect patterns like edges and textures. The activation function, usually ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit), introduces non-linearity, allowing the model to learn complex patterns. The pooling layer reduces the spatial size of the feature maps, helping to decrease computational complexity and prevent overfitting. Finally, the fully connected layer uses these extracted features to classify the image into different categories. Abstract Guardian (Human Risk Assessment & Security Awareness – HRASA) is an AI-assisted cybersecurity system designed to address one of the most critical yet overlooked aspects of organizational security—human behavior. While modern enterprises deploy advanced technical safeguards such as firewalls, SIEMs, and intrusion detection systems, a significant number of security breaches continue to occur due to human errors, including phishing attacks, weak password practices, unsafe file handling, and negligence toward security warnings. The proposed system continuously monitors user activities in real time and analyzes behavior patterns to identify potentially risky actions. Using a rule-based and AI-driven risk evaluation approach, HRASA assigns a dynamic Human Risk Score to each user based on their actions and contextual factors. When risky behavior is detected, the system provides immediate, context-aware alerts and actionable guidance to help users avoid security incidents before they occur. Guardian also includes an administrative dashboard that offers comprehensive visibility into organizational human-risk posture by highlighting high-risk users, frequently occurring risky behaviors, and trend-based risk analytics. By combining proactive monitoring, real-time alerts, and awareness-driven feedback, HRASA enhances cybersecurity resilience by reducing incidents caused by human error and promoting better security hygiene within organizations. Keywords Guardian, HRASA, Human Risk Assessment, Cyber Security Awareness, User Behavior Monitoring, Human Risk Score, Real-Time Alerts, Insider Threat Prevention, AI in Cybersecurity

Abstract Insider threats remain a critical challenge in organizational cybersecurity, given the trusted access insiders possess and the subtle nature of their malicious or negligent actions. This paper presents “A Behaviour-Driven Approach to Insider Threat Detection in Organizational Systems”, which leverages behavioural analytics to identify anomalies in user activity that may indicate potential insider threats. The proposed system establishes dynamic behavioural baselines for individual users by monitoring patterns such as access frequency, file usage, login times, and resource interactions. Any significant deviation from these baselines is flagged through a risk-scoring mechanism that aids security teams in assessing and responding to threats in real time. Unlike traditional rule-based systems, this behaviour-driven model adapts continuously to evolving user behaviour, thereby reducing false positives and enhancing detection reliability. The study includes a detailed evaluation of real-world insider threat incidents, with a focus on Indian organizations, and compares the effectiveness of current detection techniques across key metrics such as accuracy, false positive rate, and operational success. The integration of [NAME] techniques further strengthens the system’s predictive capabilities and supports automated threat mitigation strategies. By aligning behavioural intelligence with adaptive detection mechanisms, this approach provides a scalable and proactive solution to safeguard organizational systems against insider threats. Keywords: Insider Threat Detection, Behavioural Analytics, Anomaly Detection, [NAME], Adaptive Security.

Introduction Generative Adversarial networks are a deep learning model known as GAN’s, it is used for generating data such as faces, audios, animals, anime, cartoon characters, etc.[1] It is built of a generator model that is trained to generate images, and a discriminator model that classifies the output of the generator whether they are real or fake by returning a probability as a number between zero and one. Problem Statement In many criminal investigations lacking photographic or video evidence, law enforcement relies heavily on eyewitness accounts translated into facial sketches by forensic artists. This traditional process is subjective, dependent on the artist’s skill and eyewitness accuracy, time-consuming, and not scalable for rapid suspect identification. Human memory imperfections and communication gaps often lead to inaccurate sketches, causing misidentifications or investigation delays. To address these challenges, this project aims to develop an intelligent system using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to automatically convert sketches into realistic facial photographs and vice versa, reducing reliance on manual sketching while improving consistency and scalability. The primary goal of this project is to address these challenges by developing an intelligent, system that can reconstruct realistic facial photographs from sketches and vice versa using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs).

Objectives: To build a system that accurately converts sketches to photos and vice versa. To reduce manual effort and errors in facial sketching. To support real-world police investigations through intelligent automation. The scope of this project encompasses the design, development, training, and evaluation of a system that uses Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to convert facial sketches into realistic photographs and vice versa.

Methodology The proposed project will implement a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based system to perform facial sketch-to-photo and photo-to-sketch translation, specifically for law enforcement use. The theoretical foundation of this approach lies in deep learning and image-to-image translation techniques, which have seen growing success in tasks like photo enhancement, style transfer, and image reconstruction. The system then moves into the model training phase. Two types of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are employed: Pix2Pix and CycleGAN. Pix2Pix is used when paired images are available—it maps sketches directly to photos. In contrast, CycleGAN is used when paired data is limited or unavailable. It employs a cycle-consistency loss to ensure the system can reconstruct the original input from the translated output, thus maintaining identity integrity. The models are trained using the Adam optimizer with tuned learning rates and batch sizes. The training phase includes constant monitoring through metrics such as loss reduction, PSNR, and SSIM.[1] During testing, sketches unseen by the model are used to generate facial reconstructions. The outputs are post-processed for sharpening and contrast enhancement to make them clearer for human interpretation. The reconstructed images are evaluated quantitatively and qualitatively. Throughout the process, special attention is given to ensure that facial attributes such as eye spacing, jawline, and nose shape are preserved, as these are critical for identification. This method aims to reduce the dependency on subjective human sketches while increasing the accuracy, speed, and scalability of facial recognition in law enforcement settings.[8]

System Architecture The architecture of the proposed system is based on a modular design that enables input preprocessing, generative modeling, post-processing, and evaluation. At the core of this architecture is a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), composed of two competing neural networks—a Generator and a Discriminator. The Generator is responsible for creating realistic photo images from sketches (or vice versa), while the Discriminator tries to distinguish real images from generated ones, creating a feedback loop that improves output quality over time. The architecture follows an encoder-decoder style image-to-image translation pipeline. A GAN framework is used, where the generator takes in facial sketches and produces photorealistic face images. The discriminator then evaluates the authenticity of the generated images by comparing them to real photos. Conditional GANs (cGANs) are preferred here, as they allow conditioning the generation process on the input sketch image.[1][2] In the context of the sketch-to-image task, the generator learns a mapping from sketch domain S to photo. The generator is trained to fool the discriminator, resulting in increasingly realistic outputs. This adversarial process allows the model to learn high-frequency features that improve image sharpness and realism.[9][10] To improve the perceptual quality and detail of generated faces, additional loss functions like pixel-level L1 loss and perceptual loss (calculated using features from pretrained networks like VGG19) are used alongside the standard adversarial loss. Cycle-GAN: The goal of image-to-image translation is to learn the mapping between an input image and an output image by using a training set consisting of aligned pairs of images. However, for many applications, paired data would not be available. Zhu at el. proposed Cycle-GAN [2] which learns the mappings between two types of image groups with no paired examples. Cycle-GAN considers additional terms to generate outputs close to input images using class label space and image pixel space. The system must learn two mapping functions G: X->Y and F: X->Y. For this, the system is trained using two loss functions, an adversarial loss, and a cyclic consistency loss. Data Collection and Analysis Techniques The data used for training and evaluating the sketch-to-photo reconstruction model primarily comes from facial image datasets that include sketch-photo pairs or separate real-world photo domains. For this project, the key datasets include Color FERET database, CUFS, CUFSF, and the, which enrich the model’s ability to generalize across lighting, age, and ethnicity variations. Color FERET Database – A high-resolution dataset consisting of over 11,000 images of more than 1,000 individuals, including various poses, facial expressions, and illumination settings. Though it doesn’t include sketches, it provides rich photo domain diversity for training discriminators and for Cycle-GAN's unpaired translation tasks. It is particularly useful when training the photo-to-sketch or sketch-to-photo models without strict pairwise supervision. CUFS Dataset– Contains 606 paired images of hand-drawn sketches and corresponding photos from the CUHK student dataset. The dataset containing sketch images and face images are converted to non-background or white background images. The face images’ backgrounds are removed manually for every image. They are further cropped to fit the top of the hair, bottom of the chin, and the sides of the head, to eliminate as much of the background as possible, and finally resized to a resolution of 256x256 pixels. This is done in order to match the shape of the input sketch and the output face image as closely as possible, thereby reducing the adverse effects of any mismatched pairings and to keep the dataset uniform with respect to shape. Expected Outcomes The primary expected outcome of this project is the development of a deep learning-based system that can intelligently reconstruct facial images from rough or hand-drawn sketches. The model, built using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) such as Cycle-GAN or pix2pix, will be capable of translating sketch inputs into realistic images with preserved facial structure and identity features. This system is particularly designed to assist law enforcement agencies in situations where only a suspect sketch often derived from eyewitness accounts is available for identification. One of the key deliverables will be a fully trained and optimized GAN model that can operate on standard datasets like CUFS, CUFSF, and potentially the Color FERET dataset. The model is expected to achieve high performance in terms of visual quality and accuracy. Functional GAN-Based Model: A trained Cycle-GAN or pix2pix model capable of converting facial sketches into photorealistic images with preserved identity features. High Accuracy and Quality: Improved output quality validated using metrics ensuring realistic and structurally accurate face generation. Real-World Impact: Practical application in police investigations, with additional use cases in missing persons recovery, historical image restoration, and AI-driven digital arts. Beyond law enforcement, this technology could also have broader implications in areas like digital art restoration, historical image recreation, missing person searches, and AI-assisted illustration enhancement.

Conclusion The project titled “Automated Facial Sketch Synthesis for Investigations using GANs” presents a transformative approach to assist criminal investigations by leveraging advanced deep learning techniques. By using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), the system enables automatic and highly realistic reconstruction of facial images from sketches and vice versa. This addresses a major gap in traditional forensic workflows that rely heavily on manual sketches, which are often subjective and time-consuming. Through the implementation of architectures such as Pix2Pix or CycleGAN, trained on real-world sketch-photo datasets, the project aims to deliver high-quality image translations with strong applicability in suspect identification. The system enhances accuracy, reduces human dependency, and accelerates investigative processes. Overall, this project not only contributes to the field of AI-driven forensics but also aligns with real-world law enforcement needs by improving the efficiency, reliability, and accessibility of facial reconstruction tools.

Future Scope The proposed project, “Automated Facial Sketch Synthesis for Investigations using GANs”, holds significant potential for expansion and real-world impact beyond its initial implementation. Integration with social media platforms presents a strategic opportunity, given their status as comprehensive data repositories. This synergy would augment matching precision while accelerating identification workflows. Cross-Domain Generalization: The model can be extended to handle various artistic or forensic sketch styles across different cultures, demographics, and ages. Use of Advanced GAN Variants: Future iterations can adopt newer GAN architectures such as StyleGAN, StarGAN, or diffusion-based models for more realistic outputs and better feature retention.

1. Introduction In the digital age, people express their thoughts freely across platforms like Twitter, Reddit, and forums. These platforms are gold mines of public sentiment that, when mined appropriately, can offer valuable insights into how communities react to world events, products, movies, or social issues. The exponential growth of online communities has transformed social platforms into digital reflections of public sentiment. Among them, Reddit stands out as a hub where users share uncensored thoughts on a wide array of topics. This project, titled “[NAME]: A Web-Based Tool for Real-Time Reddit Sentiment & Emotion Analysis”, leverages the power of Natural Language Processing (NLP), machine learning, and data visualization to analyser public sentiment and emotional tone of Reddit comments. Users can either perform live analysis by entering keywords and subreddits, or select from pre-analyzed datasets for quick insights. The platform supports both sentiment polarity (positive, neutral, negative) and emotion detection (joy, anger, sadness, fear, surprise, etc.). The system aims to aid market researchers, analysts, students, and social scientists in understanding crowd perspectives. [NAME] ensures user accessibility through a clean UI, offers scalable backend processing, and combines real-time data streaming with fast local analysis. The system architecture is modular and can be extended with future integrations like multilingual support and trend forecasting. Reddit, known for its anonymity and community-driven content, allows deep dives into niche and trending discussions. However, Reddit lacks native analytical tools to measure user emotions or sentiments. This project bridges that gap by developing a web-based sentiment and emotion analysis system tailored specifically for Reddit. [NAME] enables users to monitor and analyze the emotional tone of Reddit comments in real time, focusing on two modes: Live Mode: Pulls and analyzes recent Reddit comments from user-input topics and subreddits. Pre-analyzed Mode: Users select from curated datasets for instant insights. This solution serves both research and commercial purposes, allowing data-driven understanding of public opinion.

2. Literature Review The rise of social media platforms like Reddit has spurred significant academic interest in content moderation, sentiment analysis, and misinformation detection. Numerous studies have leveraged machine learning models particularly deep learning architectures such as BERT, RoBERTa, and LSTM—to classify toxicity, hate speech, and misinformation. These models show high accuracy in detecting harmful content but often operate as black boxes, offering little transparency in their decision-making. Research Gap Even with many Reddit analysis research studies, they address Machine Learning-based classification, blockchain-secured traceability, XAI explainability, or adaptive moderation in silos. For example, sentiment frameworks tend to combine ML and XAI—utilizing methods such as SHAP, LIME, or even LLMs for interpretable outputs. Independent research streams cover immutable blockchain-based audit trails or federated learning models for distributed toxicity detection. However, end-to-end integration of all four pillars—ML, XAI, blockchain-based integrity, and automated moderation—is very uncommon. The majority of current Reddit analyzers remain black boxes, offering little clarity on why labels are assigned—only a few combine ML with XAI to reveal the reasoning behind outputs. And notably, almost none implement an adaptive moderation mechanism to auto-correct after detecting misinformation or user manipulation. Some community-specific models occasionally mention retraining, but rarely link it with classification logic or broader interpretability. Therefore, there's a definite gap: no real-world, lightweight Reddit analyzer offers real-time ML insights, transparent XAI explanations, tamper-proof blockchain logging, and automated moderation all together. A unified framework could bridge this gap directly—delivering a comprehensive, practical solution built for dynamic, large-scale, and evolving Reddit environments. Although recent research into Reddit comment analysis has explored a number of promising directions, the majority of current solutions remain fragmented—treating aspects like sentiment detection, content traceability, or model transparency in isolation. Many studies apply machine learning for toxicity or spam detection, while others experiment with blockchain to ensure post authenticity or trace edits. Some efforts incorporate Explainable AI (XAI) to improve interpretability, but typically only in controlled or limited settings.

As Reddit continues to grow as a major platform for discussions across diverse domains—ranging from politics and finance to health, technology, and social issues—the risk of misinformation, toxicity, and coordinated manipulation increases substantially. The platform’s open, fast-paced, and large-scale nature poses unique challenges for moderation and trustworthiness. Existing analytical systems often lack real-time adaptability, transparency in decision-making, and resilience against evolving adversarial behavior. Traditional models fall short in delivering interpretable, robust, and self-adaptive analysis necessary for responsible content governance. Most existing solutions lack the capability to provide transparent, interpretable outputs or adapt autonomously to evolving content threats. This is especially problematic in sensitive domains on Reddit—such as public health, political discourse, or financial advice—where timely and trustworthy moderation is crucial. Furthermore, the absence of integrated data integrity mechanisms like blockchain weakens the reliability, traceability, and accountability of comment histories, making the platform more susceptible to manipulation and misinformation. Therefore, the demand for an intelligent, end-to-end, and self-adaptive Reddit analysis framework is well justified. Such a system would integrate real-time content classification, explainable AI for decision transparency, secure and traceable data management via blockchain, and automated moderation or retraining—effectively bridging the gap left by traditional approaches and enabling more resilient, transparent, and trustworthy social media ecosystems. 3.1 Goals of the Project: To develop a responsive web platform for Reddit sentiment and emotion analysis. 1. Abstract Medical imaging plays a vital role in modern healthcare by enabling the diagnosis and monitoring of a wide range of diseases using modalities such as X-rays, MRI, and CT scans. Conventional diagnostic practices rely predominantly on manual interpretation by medical experts, which can be time-intensive, subjective, and susceptible to human error due to increasing patient loads and the growing complexity of medical images. Although recent advancements in deep learning particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in automated medical image analysis, most existing AI-based diagnostic systems are designed to detect only a single disease. This limitation restricts their applicability in realworld clinical environments, where patients may present with multiple coexisting conditions. Moreover, the black-box nature of many deep learning models reduces interpretability, thereby limiting clinical trust and adoption. To address these challenges, this project proposes MedAssist AI: a Multi-Disease Medical Diagnosis System, a unified and intelligent framework capable of detecting and classifying multiple diseases from medical images within a single system. The proposed approach utilizes CNN-based transfer learning models to extract robust and discriminative features from medical images, enabling accurate multi-class disease classification while reducing training time and computational cost. To enhance transparency and clinical reliability, Explainable AI (XAI) techniques such as heatmap visualizations are incorporated to highlight the regions of interest that influence the model’s predictions, allowing clinicians to better understand and validate the diagnostic outcomes. In addition, the system integrates AI agents to intelligently manage and coordinate different stages of the diagnostic workflow, including image preprocessing, disease prediction, explainability generation, and clinical decision support. These agents enable modularity, scalability, and efficient task orchestration across the diagnostic pipeline. Rather than replacing healthcare professionals, MedAssist AI functions as an assistive decision-support tool that accelerates diagnosis, reduces diagnostic errors, and facilitates early disease detection. 2. Introduction Medical imaging is a critical component of modern healthcare, supporting the diagnosis and monitoring of various diseases through modalities such as X-rays and MRI scans. Traditional diagnostic processes rely heavily on manual interpretation by medical experts, which can be time-consuming, subjective, and prone to error due to increasing workloads and image complexity. Recent advancements in deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have shown strong potential in automated medical image analysis. However, most existing AI-based diagnostic systems are limited to identifying a single disease, making them unsuitable for real-world clinical scenarios where multiple conditions may coexist. Additionally, many deep learning models operate as black-box systems, providing limited interpretability, which reduces trust and acceptance among healthcare professionals. The proposed MedAssist AI Multi-Disease Medical Diagnosis System addresses these limitations by developing a unified framework capable of detecting multiple diseases from medical images within a single system. The project leverages CNN-based transfer learning models to extract discriminative features and accurately classify medical images into different disease categories. To improve transparency and clinical reliability, Explainable AI techniques such as heatmap visualizations are incorporated to highlight affected regions influencing the model’s predictions. Furthermore, the system integrates AI agents to intelligently manage and coordinate different stages of the diagnostic pipeline, including image preprocessing, disease classification, explainability generation, and decision support. Rather than replacing medical professionals, the system functions as a decision support tool, assisting clinicians in faster diagnosis, reducing diagnostic errors, and enabling early disease detection. This approach demonstrates how agent-based AI and deep learning can be effectively combined to enhance modern healthcare outcomes. 4

3. Literature Survey 
The literature survey is organized into three major categories: (i) agent-based clinical decision support systems, (ii) multi-label disease prediction using machine learning, and (iii) hybrid intelligent systems combining agents, learning, and medical knowledge 3.1 Agent-Based Medical Diagnosis and Decision Support Systems Early research emphasized the use of multi-agent systems (MAS) to model complex, distributed medical environments where multiple stakeholders (patients, physicians, nurses, databases) interact dynamically. Oprea proposed MEDICAL MAS, an agent-based system designed to support medical diagnosis through cooperation among personal agents and information-searching agents The architecture includes physician agents, patient agents, nurse agents, and information retrieval agents that collectively access relational medical databases. The physician agent employs rule-based reasoning with confidence factors to infer diagnoses and treatment plans. This system demonstrated how MAS can enhance flexibility, autonomy, and distributed decision-making in medical diagnosis. Korolyova et al. developed a multi-agent clinical decision support system (CDSS) integrated with Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) to improve adaptability and learning from past medical cases The system architecture consists of interface, execution, and knowledge modules, with specialized agents for searching, adapting, evaluating, and coordinating decisions. Experimental evaluation on heart disease diagnosis showed improved reasoning accuracy and adaptability. Despite its strengths, the system focuses primarily on single-disease diagnosis and does not explicitly address simultaneous multi-disease prediction. Overall, agent-based approaches provide strong support for distributed reasoning, collaboration, and explainability but often lack robust data-driven learning mechanisms for complex disease interdependencies. 5 3.2 Multi-Label Disease Prediction Using Machine Learning With the increasing availability of electronic health records (EHRs), machine learning techniques particularly multi-label classification (MLC) have gained attention for diagnosing multiple diseases or complications simultaneously. Zhou et al. applied multi-label classification models to predict four diabetic complications concurrently using large scale EHR data The study compared Binary Relevance, Label Power Set, Classifier Chains, Ensemble Classifier Chains, and Calibrated Label Ranking models. Results showed that Ensemble Classifier Chains significantly outperformed traditional binary classifiers by exploiting correlations among complications. This includes implementing advanced image processing techniques to enhance quality and noise reduction, ensuring that the input for the AI models is of the highest clinical standard. 2. To Extract and Classify the Multi-Disease Feature This phase focuses on the core diagnostic engine. By leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Transfer Learning, the system generates discriminative representations of various pathologies. This allows the model to perform reliable multiclass classification, identifying several diseases within a single diagnostic workflow. 3. 7. Methodology The proposed MedAssist AI Multi-Disease Medical Diagnosis System is developed using a phased methodology to ensure systematic design, implementation, and evaluation. Each phase addresses a specific component of the system while maintaining integration through AI agent coordination. Phase 1: Data Collection and Dataset Preparation In this phase, publicly available and clinically validated medical imaging datasets are collected, including X-ray and MRI images representing multiple disease categories. The datasets are examined for class imbalance, image quality, and labelling accuracy. The data is then organized into training, validation, and testing subsets to support reliable model development and evaluation. Phase 2: Image Preprocessing and Enhancement This phase focuses on improving the quality and consistency of input images. Preprocessing operations such as resizing, normalization, noise reduction, and contrast enhancement are applied. Data augmentation techniques, including rotation, flipping, and scaling, are used to improve model generalization. A dedicated AI preprocessing agent manages and automates these tasks to ensure standardized input across the system. 11 Phase 3: Feature Extraction Using Deep Learning In this phase, Convolutional Neural Networks and transfer learning models such as ResNet, DenseNet, or EfficientNet are employed to extract discriminative features from medical images. Pre-trained models are fine-tuned on the medical datasets to capture disease specific patterns while reducing training time and overfitting. The diagnosis AI agent selects and executes the appropriate model for multi-disease classification. Phase 4: Multi-Disease Classification and Prediction The extracted features are passed to a multi-class classification layer that predicts disease categories along with confidence scores. The system is designed to handle multiple disease classes within a single framework. The diagnosis agent performs inference and forwards

results to subsequent agents for interpretation and validation. Phase 5: Explainable AI Integration To address the black-box nature of deep learning models, Explainable AI techniques such as Grad-CAM are applied in this phase. Heatmaps are generated to visually highlight regions in the medical images that influence the model’s predictions. An explainability AI agent is responsible for producing and managing these visual explanations, enhancing transparency and clinician trust. Phase 6: AI Agent-Based Decision Support In this phase, a decision support agent aggregates outputs from the diagnosis and explainability agents. It analyses confidence levels, flags uncertain predictions, and presents structured diagnostic insights through the user interface. This phase ensures that the system functions as an assistive tool for clinicians rather than an autonomous decisionmaker.

ABSTRACT Facial image synthesis has emerged as a crucial application of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), particularly in forensic investigations. This study critically examines recent GAN-based approaches and identifies key limitations that affect their effectiveness and generalizability. A major concern is the reliance on biased and limited training datasets, which significantly restrict the demographic diversity and realism of the generated outputs. Most models are trained on domain-specific or paired datasets, reducing their adaptability to real-world, hand-drawn forensic sketches. Furthermore, the lack of end-to-end training pipelines in multi-GAN architectures often compromises model stability and consistency during image generation. Additionally, the use of Cycle-GANs, while effective in some domains, suffers from poor interpretability in feature reconstruction and limited generalization when trained on small or homogeneous datasets. This report sets the foundation for advancing forensic sketch reconstruction by bridging these identified gaps through improved dataset diversity, enhanced model interpretability, and more meaningful evaluation frameworks. Keywords: GANs, Cycle-GAN, Facial Image Synthesis, Forensic Application, Image Generation.

INTRODUCTION Generative Adversarial networks are a deep learning model known as GAN’s, it is used for generating data such as faces, audios, animals, anime, cartoon characters, etc.[1] It is built of a generator model that is trained to generate images, and a discriminator model that classifies the output of the generator whether they are real or fake by returning a probability as a number between zero and one. This project proposes a system that can intelligently reconstruct or generate facial sketches from photographs and vice versa using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The purpose of this project is to support law enforcement agencies by accelerating the suspect identification process with higher accuracy and reduced dependency on human sketch artists. We propose the use of Generative Adversarial Neural Network (GAN) architecture and training model for generation of facial images. A basic GAN takes random noise (i.e. a random vector of n float numbers) as input and it transforms this noise into some meaningful output which resembles the dataset it has been trained upon. The significance of this project lies in its direct impact on improving public safety and the criminal justice system. The integration of AI in forensic sketching not only reduces the dependency on human sketch artists but also provides a scalable, consistent, and objective solution.

LITERATURE SURVEY SCOPE The project aims to develop a generative adversarial framework capable of producing high-quality, detail-preserving face sketches from real images. It emphasizes the synthesis of accurate and realistic facial sketches that retain identity-critical features, using a combination of adversarial loss and a custom detail loss function. This has applications in law enforcement, digital forensics, and artistic rendering This project proposes a system that can intelligently reconstruct or generate facial sketches from photographs and vice versa using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The purpose of this project is to support law enforcement agencies by accelerating the suspect identification process with higher accuracy and reduced dependency on human sketch artists. Key Aspects of the Project Detail Preservation A unique contribution of this work is the introduction of a detail loss function, designed to penalize the model if it loses fine details during generation. This helps in generating sketches that closely match the structural and identity-defining features of the source image. GAN Architecture Enhancement The project extends traditional GAN frameworks by integrating both adversarial loss (to ensure realism) and detail loss (to retain identity). MOTIVATION In real-world applications such as criminal investigations, surveillance, and missing person cases, face sketches often serve as critical visual cues when photographs are unavailable. However, traditional sketch generation—either manual or algorithmic—often fails to preserve fine facial details that are essential for accurate identification. This creates a pressing need for an automated system that can produce highly detailed and identity-preserving face sketches from photographs. Recent advances in Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have shown promising results in image translation tasks, but most existing models prioritize realism over structural fidelity, often blurring or distorting subtle features. To bridge this gap, this project introduces a detailpreserving GAN framework, incorporating a custom "detail loss" alongside adversarial learning. The motivation is to create sketches that not only look realistic but also retain individual facial characteristics, making them more reliable for both human interpretation and machine recognition systems. This addresses a significant challenge in forensic and biometric fields, where both accuracy and identity retention are crucial.

PROPOSED SYSTEM The proposed system aims to develop an AI-based framework capable of converting facial sketches into photo-realistic images using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). This solution is particularly tailored for law enforcement agencies to assist in suspect identification when photographic evidence is unavailable and only sketches based on eyewitness descriptions exist. At the core of the system lies a GAN architecture, such as Pix2Pix (for paired data) or CycleGAN (for unpaired data), chosen based on the nature of the dataset. The generator model is trained to convert sketches into realistic facial images, while the discriminator evaluates how closely the generated images resemble real photos. The system is developed using Python, leveraging machine learning libraries like PyTorch, TensorFlow, etc. Training is conducted on publicly available datasets such as the CUHK Face Sketch Dataset (CUFS) and CUFSF, which contain paired sketch-photo images suitable for supervised learning. Once trained, the model is integrated into a user-friendly interface that allows law enforcement officers to upload a sketch and receive a realistic facial image in return. This automated process significantly reduces reliance on forensic artists, speeds up suspect identification, and enhances investigative efficiency. The system is scalable and can also support the reverse task—generating sketches from photos—for data expansion and training purposes.

PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) Analysis PSNR measures the quality of the reconstructed image against the original. While industry benchmarks for high-fidelity compression often target the 30-50 dB range, our model's current iteration establishes a solid operational baseline. The PSNR distribution shows consistent behavior: The primary cluster of results is tightly grouped between 17 dB and 19.5 dB, with a notable peak frequency around 17.5 dB. This high consistency is a satisfactory outcome, demonstrating stable and predictable model behavior. A small number of outliers were identified at ~13.8 dB. These have been isolated and provide valuable data for targeted model refinement. This well-defined performance at ~17-19 dB provides a clear and reliable baseline from which to measure future optimization cycles. SSIM (Structural Similarity Index Measure) Analysis SSIM evaluates the perceptual similarity between two images, where a score of 1.0 represents a perfect match. ABSTRACT In the face of increasing urban crowd density, rising numbers of child disappearance cases, and the limitations of conventional surveillance systems, the need for intelligent and responsive safety solutions has never been more urgent[10]. AI Lost Tech is a real-time, AI-powered surveillance and alert system designed to assist in the rapid identification and recovery of lost or unattended children in public spaces[1],[5]. By integrating computer vision, facial recognition, and automated risk analysis into a single unified platform, the system enhances the responsiveness and reliability of child safety infrastructure[2],[3]. The primary objective of AI Lost Tech is to bridge the gap between passive surveillance and active intervention by using existing CCTV feeds and advanced AI algorithms to detect, identify, and assess the presence of lost children. Through real-time object detection and face matching with missing children’s databases, the system can quickly flag high-risk situations and alert security personnel with precise visual and location data. The application also offers a parent-initiated alert feature, enabling families to submit missing child information directly, initiating an immediate system- wide search. Abstract - The exponential growth of user-generated content on platforms like Reddit has prompted the need for intelligent moderation systems capable of operating at scale with minimal human intervention. Despite various advancements, current moderation techniques often fall short in delivering transparency, adaptability, and real-time responsiveness across diverse communities. This project, titled “Reddit Analyzer,” proposes a novel and modular framework that integrates multiple layers of intelligence to enable automated content classification, explanation, logging, and self-adaptive control for platform moderation. The system architecture comprises key modules: a Machine Learning Engine for real-time classification of harmful or misleading comments, an Explainable AI (XAI) Layer using SHAP or LIME to expose decision logic, a Blockchain-Based Logger for tamper-proof moderation history, and a Self-Adaptive Control Mechanism that enables autonomous response or retraining in the face of evolving content threats. Together, these components simulate an intelligent moderation system capable of detecting, explaining, recording, and reacting to manipulation campaigns or toxic content with minimal delay. A unique feature of the system is its modularity and scalability, designed to function efficiently across diverse subreddit environments and community rules. Moderator feedback and content patterns are continuously analyzed to improve model performance and adapt dynamically to shifting discourse trends. This includes automated reputation scoring, coordination pattern detection, and customizable dashboards for human oversight, all operating on lightweight infrastructure compatible with cloud or local deployment. To ensure robustness, the system includes safety checks and fallback mechanisms that trigger appropriate interventions during high-volume or anomalous traffic scenarios. The entire pipeline is optimized for low-latency processing, high interpretability, and auditability, aligning with the demands of modern content governance. By integrating AI-driven classification, blockchain-based traceability, and autonomous recovery protocols, the Reddit Analyzer represents a comprehensive and forward-looking solution for scalable, trustworthy moderation. It serves as a pioneering step in the convergence of machine learning, explainable AI, and secure system design for online discourse management. Existing approaches can be broadly categorized as follows: Existing sentiment and emotion analysis systems have largely focused on general-purpose social media platforms such as Twitter and Facebook, with limited emphasis on Reddit. Traditional approaches rely on lexicon-based methods such as VADER and LIWC, which are lightweight and optimized for short, informal text. These systems perform reasonably well on tweets or microblogs but struggle with Reddit’s long-form discussions, sarcasm, and context-dependent expressions. More recent advances employ deep learning models such as BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT, which achieve state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets like SST and GoEmotions. However, many of these transformer-based systems are designed for offline batch processing, making them unsuitable for real-time analysis at scale. Commercial social media monitoring platforms, such as Brandwatch or Hootsuite Insights, also offer sentiment analysis, but their support for Reddit is either minimal or lacks critical features such as thread-level context, subreddit-specific filtering, and fine-grained emotion tracking. Meanwhile, streaming analytics frameworks like Apache Kafka or Spark Streaming provide the infrastructure for handling large volumes of data in real time, yet they require significant customization and domain-specific adaptation to work effectively with Reddit’s unique community-driven content. Overall, existing systems fail to capture the complexities of Reddit’s ecosystem. They either lack accuracy in handling Reddit’s linguistic variety or fail to provide real-time, interactive tools for sentiment and emotion monitoring. Abstract: - 
Tuberculosis (TB) is still a major infectious disease which we are 
fighting at global scale and we require for it prompt and accurate 
diagnosis to breaks its transmission and to improve patient results. 
Presently we use traditional screening methods like sputum 
microscopy and manual interpretation of Chest X-rays (CXRs) 
which are very labor intensive, time consuming and also, we see 
great variation between readers which in turn affects the result 
especially in resource poor settings. In this work we put forth a full 
scale deep learning based system for automatic TB detection and 
also, we aim to make the AI which is now a “black box” -- open. We 
preprocess public chest x ray sets and then we use Deep 
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for strong feature 
extraction and classification. To solve the issue of standard AI 
models which are black box in nature we introduce Explainable AI 
(XAI) which we use Grad-CAM to visualized the infected areas. 
Also to close the gap between what we technically diagnose and 
what the patient understands we have put in a LLaMA-3 driven 
conversational AI which issues out medical reports in a human 
friendly language and also answers questions. We evaluate 
performance of the model to prove out its reliability. This study 
reports our work which is to present a transparent, intelligent and 
interactive tool for TB diagnosis via the use of this platform which 
in turn we hope will improve efficiency of clinical workflows. Keywords— Deep Learning, Tuberculosis, X-ray Analysis, 
Explainable AI, LLaMA-3, Grad-CAM, Medical Image

bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It mostly affects the 
lungs but can affect other parts of the body as well. TB is 
curable, but lack of access to health care in poor countries 
makes TB one of the biggest killers in the world. The early 
days of set detection is critical to improving outcomes. The 
challenges of identifying TB is the reliance on chest x-rays 
which requires the expertise of a radiologist. This is often the 
case for many rural and poor communities. [1].

intelligence (XAI) for visual transparency with transfer learning 
for precise classification. Furthermore, given the importance of 
automated documentation in healthcare, we have utilized

Result In this study, the performance of the proposed Convolutional 
Neural Network (CNN) model was evaluated for tuberculosis 
detection using chest X-ray images. The model was trained and 
validated using the prepared dataset, and its performance was 
assessed using standard classification metrics including accuracy, 
precision, recall, and F1-score. The experimental results 
demonstrate that the proposed CNN model achieved a validation 
accuracy of 93.0%, indicating strong capability in distinguishing 
between tuberculosis-positive and normal chest X-ray images. 
The high accuracy reflects the effectiveness of the model in 
learning discriminative features from medical images. To further 
validate the performance of the proposed approach, a 
comparative analysis was conducted with well-known deep 
learning architectures such as ResNet50, MobileNetV2, and 
EfficientNetB0. The comparison results show that the proposed 
CNN model outperformed these architectures in terms of 
validation accuracy while maintaining lower computational 
complexity and fewer parameters. Specifically, ResNet50 
achieved an accuracy of 90.8%, MobileNetV2 achieved 91.6%, 
and EfficientNetB0 achieved 92.1%. In contrast, the proposed 
CNN model achieved the highest accuracy of 93.0%, 
demonstrating its superior performance for the given dataset.

Introduction SpindleOne is an integrated management suite developed to digitize and streamline operational workflows in small and medium manufacturing enterprises. It provides a unified web-based platform to manage finance, supply chain, and people-related activities efficiently, serving as a digital gateway that synchronizes disparate data sources like manual entries and historical CSVs.
The current implementation focuses on the SpindleFinance module, which enables structured cash-flow tracking, transaction recording, and real-time balance monitoring. This implementation serves as a foundation for future predictive analytics and decision-support features proposed under the MFG360 framework, such as identifying behavioral patterns and predicting payment delays at a "Deal-Level". Unified Web Platform: Centralized access to enterprise operations, including Finance, Supply, and People management, through a single web interface.
Real-Time Cash-Flow Visibility: Instant tracking of inflows and outflows via a centralized "Cashflow" table and "Add New Record" feature to monitor account balances.
SME-Oriented Predictive Foundation: Designed to capture granular transaction details required for Temporal Feature Engineering and proactive liquidity forecasting in resource-constrained enterprises. Motivation Manufacturing SMEs commonly depend on manual bookkeeping or fragmented digital tools for managing financial transactions. This leads to poor visibility of cash inflows and outflows, delayed payment tracking, and a higher possibility of errors in financial records.
Due to the absence of centralized financial dashboards, business owners often rely on retrospective reports rather than real-time insights. This reactive approach makes it difficult to assess liquidity positions and respond promptly to financial risks.
The motivation of this project is to transform raw and unorganized transaction data into a structured and centralized financial system. By enabling systematic cash-flow tracking and real-time monitoring, the system supports informed decision-making and establishes a base for future predictive financial analytics.

Problem Statement Despite the increasing adoption of digital payment systems and accounting tools, financial management in small manufacturing enterprises remains inefficient due to the lack of integrated, real-time analytics solutions. Key challenges include: • Financial data is often scattered across manual records, spreadsheets, and disconnected digital tools, leading to poor data consistency and limited visibility.
• Most existing systems generate static and retrospective reports, such as ledgers and aging statements, which do not support real-time cash-flow monitoring.
• Transaction-level and deal-level payment behavior is not captured, preventing accurate assessment of liquidity risk and delayed payments.
• There is a lack of centralized, analytics-ready platforms that integrate data entry, monitoring, visualization, and future predictive modeling in a scalable manner.

ABSTRACT Traditional cyber threat detection systems rely on centralized data collection and analysis, 
making them vulnerable to privacy breaches, data leakage, and regulatory compliance issues. 
This project introduces a privacy-preserving cyber threat detection framework using 
Federated Learning (FL) that enables collaborative model training across multiple 
distributed clients without sharing raw sensitive data. 
The system supports local model training on network traffic and security logs at individual 
client nodes, while only encrypted model parameters are transmitted to a central aggregation

highest standards of data confidentiality and user privacy.

ABSTRACT Millions of people it is very difficult to apply for important government documents like income certificates, caste certificates, and proof of domicile, especially if they live in rural areas or have limited digital skills in India. Dispersed portals, unclear instructions, inconsistent state-by-state procedures, and district-level these all factors complicate the process. These problems often result in process errors, frequent office visits, and the exclusion of less technical expertized individuals. We have developed GovGuideBot, an AI-powered chat-bot that explains government documentation procedures, to address this issue. It pro-vides easy-to-use, location-based, step-by-step assistance. In order to under-stand user intent, the system uses a Natural Language Processing (NLP) pipeline that is optimized with transform-er models like BERT. Named [NAME] (NER) is used to identify crucial information such as document type, state, and district. These specifics are arranged in structured JSON workflows that enable region-specific instructions. GovGuideBot also uses location entered by user query to adapt procedures for user locations, links to official government websites to guarantee accuracy, and uses the YouTube Data API to offer visual tutorials which are particularly useful for users who might have literacy issues or are using these services for the first time. With a precision of 91%, a recall of 93%, and an overall F1-score of 92% for identifying intents and entities, GovGuideBot performs well when tested on actual citizen questions. About half of the planned features were successfully implemented in the working prototype we created for Maharashtra, which includes workflows for income, caste, and domicile certificates. By supporting multiple languages and media formats, GovGuideBot demonstrates how chatbot technology can improve access for more people, decrease needless visits to service sites, and reduce procedural errors. 6 CONCLUSION The article discusses an AI-enabled conversational agent named GovGuideBot, which is aimed to enhance the process of applying for government documents such as Income, Caste, and Domicile Certification, through one-on-one assistance based on location and process, natural language processing (NLP), and machine learning. GovGuideBot illustrates an understanding of the challenges faced by citizens, especially for individuals in rural areas or those with very low digital literacy, when attempting to gain access to fundamental government services. The results of the evaluation found that GovGuideBot had a very high accuracy of 92% for intent recognition, an average response time of 1.4 seconds, and a 35% decrease in the number of errors on applications (as compared to self-guidance processes). Personalized feedback from participants also conveyed that GovGuideBot improved clarity, reduced stove piping of official documentation, and decreased reliance on informal agents or blogs for additional information. In addition to enhancing access to services GovGuideBot also supports larger Digital India initiatives, which include increasing citizen engagement, reducing congestion at the government office, and provides the opportunity for those that are less digitally literate to engage digitally. GovGuideBot is modular and built to grow in future applications, including more regional language support and developments where voice can also be included for users. The application has also great potential for unique IoT-enabled features such as tracking of the queue for offices in real-time or tracking the delivery of documents. In summary, GovGuideBot represents an actionable, scalable, and citizen-focused implementation of e-governance. GovGuideBot is at the intersection of policy intention and citizen experience on the ground. GovGuideBot has the potential to be a consistently repeatable model to improve public service delivery not only in India but in many parts of the world more broadly as they face similar administrative barriers.

ABSTRACT GarudVyuha addresses the primary limitations of conventional unmanned aerial vehicles that rely on centralized control and manual triggering. In high-risk missions such as defense surveillance, reconnaissance, or disaster response, these systems are highly vulnerable to jamming and command loss. This research introduces a self- triggered autonomous swarm drone framework, where each drone activates independently using onboard sensors such as the MPU6050 upon deployment or free fall. This mechanism enables instant mid-air activation without human input, ensuring mission continuity even if the mothership or ground control fails. The system integrates Pixhawk-based flight control, LoRa communication, and AI-powered FPV vision modules to achieve real-time coordination, target detection, and adaptive response. The proposed design incorporates a mechanical latch-and-release system that safely deploys multiple child drones, each programmed to self-initiate and disperse for assigned functions. Experimental validation demonstrates robust self- triggering, reliable communication, and formation stability under signal-degraded conditions. Future developments include reinforcement learning for adaptive formations, multi-agent communication optimization, and field-level deployment. Overall, GarudVyuha represents a significant step toward resilient, intelligent, and fully autonomous aerial swarm systems for next-generation defense and disaster management. text: Abstract— Children with dyslexia often struggle with alphabet recognition, phonemic awareness, and associating letters with sounds and images. This paper presents a prototype Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) system designed to support dyslexic learners aged 5–10 years. The VR module allows students to type alphabets, see the letter visually, hear its pronunciation, and view a corresponding image. The AR module uses a custom Android application to scan printed book images, overlay 3D objects on them, play audio cues, and display short descriptions. We conducted a pilot study with three dyslexic students and two teachers from a specialized NGO. Results show improved engagement and faster letter recognition in VR compared to AR, with overall positive feedback from teachers. This work demonstrates the potential of AR/VR to create a multisensory learning environment that caters to diverse cognitive needs. Keywords— Dyslexia Support, AR/VR Learning, Multisensory Education, Inclusive Learning, Early Literacy Empowerment

text: Introduction Dyslexia affects nearly 10–15% of children globally, making it one of the most common neurodevelopmental disorders. Children with dyslexia face difficulties in decoding words, recognizing letters, and processing written language, which can lead to lower academic performance and reduced self-esteem. Conventional teaching methods rely heavily on written text and rote memorization, which increases cognitive strain for dyslexic learners. Recent advances in immersive technologies such as AR and VR have created new opportunities for inclusive education. These tools enable students to learn through multiple senses—visual, auditory, and kinesthetic—rather than depending solely on text. Immersive classrooms can help children form stronger symbol-sound associations, visualize phonics, and interact with objects in a way that improves comprehension and retention.This paper presents the design, development, and evaluation of an AR/VR-based learning platform specifically tailored for dyslexic learners, aiming to make education more engaging, inclusive, and accessible. Background and Motivation Dyslexia affects nearly 10–15% of school-aged children worldwide, causing significant challenges in reading, writing, and language processing. Conventional teaching methods rely heavily on text-based content, which increases cognitive strain for dyslexic learners and can hinder concept retention. Recent research suggests that immersive, multisensory learning environments can significantly improve literacy skills by leveraging spatial memory, visual association, and auditory reinforcement. Need of Immersive Learning Platform Immersive AR/VR technologies provide a unique opportunity to overcome the limitations of traditional methods by creating an engaging, low-stress learning environment. VR simulations allow students to interact with alphabets and objects in 3D, improving their symbol recognition and phonics comprehension. AR enhances real-world learning by overlaying interactive objects on physical environments, enabling contextual learning and memory retention. By focusing on inclusivity and affordability, the platform can be scaled for use in classrooms with limited technological infrastructure. Proposed Approach

Passig [10] used immersive VR experiences to improve educators’ awareness of the cognitive challenges faced by dyslexic students, encouraging empathy-based instructional design. Collectively, these studies highlight that immersive technologies, when integrated with inclusive design principles, can significantly enhance literacy outcomes, engagement, and confidence for neurodiverse learner.

text: METHODOLOGY The proposed system of the AR/VR-based learning platform aims to enhance early literacy skills for dyslexic students by combining immersive virtual reality training and interactive augmented reality experiences. Dyslexic learners often struggle with recognizing letters, associating them with words, and recalling phonetic sounds, which can hinder reading and writing development. The VR module was designed to provide an interactive 3D environment where students could physically engage with alphabet objects, reinforcing letter recognition through manipulation and audio feedback. Simultaneously, the AR module was tailored to allow students to scan textbook images and interact with corresponding 3D models, helping bridge the gap between physical learning materials and digital reinforcement. text: RESULT AND ANALYSIS The performance of the AR/VR learning platform was evaluated using a combination of quantitative metrics and user feedback surveys. Metrics were designed to measure accuracy, engagement, learning gain, and usability. Alphabet Placement Accuracy (VR Module): Measures the percentage of 3D objects correctly placed into the box by students. Task Completion Time: Measures the average time (in seconds) taken by students to pick and place a single alphabet object. The average engagement index across 10 students was 4.6/5, showing high interest and involvement in both VR and AR modules. Learning Gain (Pre-Test vs Post-Test): Assesses improvement in alphabet recognition after using the system. Students’ average pre-test score: 62% Students’ average post-test score: 89% Average Learning Gain: 27%, demonstrating substantial improvement in letter recognition. Technical Performance Evaluation 1.VR Module Interaction. The VR module demonstrated a high level of accuracy, with 94% of alphabet placements correctly completed by students. Each 3D object representing a letter (A–Z) could be picked up and placed in the virtual box using VR controllers. Sequential triggers in Unity ensured that once a letter was correctly placed, an audio cue confirmed the success (“Correct! A for Apple”) and automatically spawned the next letter. This design allowed students to progress smoothly through the alphabet without confusion, maintaining engagement and minimizing errors. 2.AR Module Recognition. The AR module, built using Unity with Vuforia Engine and ARCore, successfully recognized 96% of the textbook images scanned by students. When an image target was detected, the corresponding 3D model appeared on the screen along with an audio description. This accurate detection allowed students to interact with objects in real-time, reinforcing the learning of letter–object associations. Even with variations in lighting and device angles, the image recognition remained reliable.

The objects were responsive, with smooth movement and no lag, ensuring an intuitive and immersive experience. This capability also helped students with dyslexia who benefit from multisensory and interactive learning methods. 4.Audio Response Time. Both the VR and AR modules provided immediate audio feedback, with response times under 1 second. This quick feedback reinforced learning by linking actions directly to sounds, helping students remember letter pronunciations and object associations. Real-time audio reinforcement proved essential for keeping the learning experience engaging and effective for young learners. Ease of Use: All four students reported that the VR and AR modules were intuitive and easy to navigate. The sequential tasks in VR, where objects had to be placed in the box in order, were especially appreciated for helping them focus on one letter at a time without feeling overwhelmed. Clarity of Instructions: Students found the audio instructions and prompts clear and easy to follow. The combination of visual cues (3D objects, AR models) and verbal guidance helped students understand each task quickly. They indicated that the instructions were more understandable than traditional text-based classroom materials.

1. Introduction In modern fruit farming, maintaining plant health is critical to ensuring optimal yield and quality. However, early detection of crop diseases—particularly those affecting leaves such as wilting and nematode infestations—remains a significant challenge. These diseases often go unnoticed until severe damage has occurred, resulting in reduced productivity and financial losses. To address this, there is a growing need for intelligent, automated solutions that can accurately classify fruit crop diseases at an early stage using minimal resources. The project titled:
“Fruit Crop Disease Classification using Quantum Machine Learning on IBM Quantum Cloud”
proposes a novel system that combines the strengths of artificial intelligence and quantum computing to detect and classify fruit crop health conditions. The core objective is to classify fruit leaf images into three key categories: Healthy Wilting Nematode-Infected This classification process allows farmers, researchers, and agronomists to take informed actions quickly, improving disease management and crop care strategies. Unlike traditional machine learning models—which often require large datasets, high-performance GPUs, and long training cycles—this project adopts Quantum Machine Learning (QML) to reduce training time and computational complexity, making it ideal for real-time deployment in rural or low-resource settings. The workflow includes: Input: Grayscale images of fruit leaves captured via smartphones or field cameras. Preprocessing: Each image is resized and converted to grayscale, then passed through Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to reduce its dimensionality. Quantum Encoding: The reduced features are encoded into quantum circuits using rotation gates (RY) and entanglement. Quantum Neural Network (QNN): Built using IBM's Qiskit, this model learns patterns in the data to classify the leaf as healthy, wilted, or nematode-infected. Execution: The model runs on IBM Quantum Cloud hardware or simulators depending on availability. Frontend: A user-friendly interface built with Streamlit lets users upload an image and receive instant crop health classification results. 2.Literature Review

Recent studies show Quantum Machine Learning (QML), especially QNNs, can classify with fewer resources and faster training. Combining PCA with QML offers a promising, efficient alternative for agricultural image classification. Fig.2.1 Literature Survey Research Gap Numerous studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of traditional machine learning (ML) algorithms in plant disease detection. For instance, Singh et al. applied classical ML to detect multiple diseases in apple leaves, while Patankar and Moon focused on wilt detection in radish using conventional image processing techniques. Although these approaches achieve reasonable accuracy, they often require large datasets, high computational resources, and lack scalability for field deployment in resource-constrained environments. Recent advances in quantum computing have inspired hybrid models and theoretical comparisons. Katirci et al. conducted a comparative study of classical vs. quantum ML on sugar beet disease but primarily evaluated performance metrics without implementing full quantum training pipelines. Similarly, Alam et al. explored quantum-classical hybrid models for image classification, but their focus remained on benchmark datasets without crop-specific adaptation. Works like Anand et al. introduced quantum-inspired feature selection (QEFS), and Sudha et al. proposed quantum-enhanced diagnosis for tomato leaves, highlighting quantum potential, but lacked complete application pipelines for multi-disease classification in fruit crops. Despite these advancements, there is a clear research gap in developing an end-to-end, quantum-enhanced disease classification system tailored for fruit crops, especially for distinguishing between diseases like wilting and nematode infections. No existing study combines grayscale image preprocessing, PCA-based feature compression, quantum neural networks (QNN) with real qubit execution (IBM Quantum Cloud), and an interactive frontend interface.

3. Problem Statement Fruit crop diseases like wilting and nematode infections often go undetected in their early stages, leading to significant losses for farmers. While traditional machine learning models can help with image-based disease detection, they require large datasets, powerful hardware, and long training times, making them impractical for real-time use in rural or low-resource environments. This project addresses the issue by developing a Quantum Machine Learning (QML) model that classifies grayscale images of fruit leaves into three categories—healthy, wilting, and nematode-infected—using dimensionality reduction with PCA and a Quantum Neural Network executed on IBM’s Quantum Cloud. The aim is to enable faster, resource-efficient, and accurate disease detection to support sustainable and smart farming practices.

Objectives of the Project The main objective of this project is to build a Quantum Machine Learning-based system that can accurately classify fruit crop leaf images into three health conditions: healthy, wilting, and nematode-infected. The goal is to reduce the training time and computational resources required for classification, compared to traditional machine learning methods, while improving accuracy and making disease detection more accessible for farmers and agricultural researchers. Comparative Study of Algorithms : Classical models like CNN, SVM, and Random Forest were considered, but we selected Quantum Neural Network (QNN) for its faster training, fewer parameters, better performance on small datasets, and future scalability with quantum hardware. Methodology The proposed system follows a multi-stage pipeline that integrates image preprocessing, dimensionality reduction, quantum feature encoding, variational quantum circuit training, and interactive result visualization. The methodology focuses on automating the classification of fruit crop health by converting raw crop leaf images into compact, quantum-encodable feature vectors using PCA, encoding these features into quantum circuits with rotation and entanglement gates, and executing quantum neural network inference on IBM Quantum Cloud. The system further provides a user-friendly frontend interface for real-time image upload, disease prediction, and visualization of classification results, thereby enabling fast, accurate, and scalable crop health diagnosis.

System Architecture The system consists of the following core modules: Image Input Layer Users upload fruit leaf images (PNG / JPG) through a simple drag-and-drop or file selection interface. Basic metadata such as filename, image resolution, user ID, and timestamp are recorded for tracking and auditing purposes. Image Preprocessing and Feature Extraction Module Uploaded images are converted to grayscale and resized (e.g., 64×64) to reduce complexity. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is applied to extract 4–8 principal components, compressing the image data into low-dimensional feature vectors compatible with quantum circuit encoding. Quantum Circuit Encoding and Model Training Module The PCA-reduced feature vectors are encoded as rotation angles in parameterized quantum gates (e.g., RY gates) within a variational quantum circuit. Entanglement operations (CNOT gates) create correlations between qubits. The quantum neural network (QNN) model is trained using classical optimizers (such as COBYLA or SPSA) on IBM Quantum Cloud real hardware or Aer simulators. Prediction and Evaluation Module Trained QNN models classify input images into categories: Healthy, Wilting, or Nematode-Infected.
Outputs include predicted class probabilities and confidence scores. Model performance metrics (accuracy, confusion matrix) are computed to validate and compare results with classical CNN baselines. Algorithm Workflow Input Acquisition : User upload fruit crop leaf image through the web interface. Image PreProcessing : Convert the image to grayscale, resize to a fixed dimension, and normalize pixel values. Feature Extraction : Apply Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to reduce the image to 4–8 principal components. Quantum Encoding : Encode PCA feature values as rotation angles in a parameterized quantum circuit using rotation gates Quantum Neural Network Training : Train the variational quantum circuit using classical optimizers (COBYLA/SPSA) on IBM Quantum Cloud or simulator. Prediction : Run inference on new images to classify the crop health status (Healthy, Wilting, Nematode-Infected).

Result Visualization : Display predicted class labels, confidence scores, and quantum circuit details on the frontend interface. Technologies and Tools Data & Functional Testing Input Data: Fruit crop leaf images uploaded in standard formats such as PNG or JPG.
